# Security, Auth, Quota & Failover Checklist: Unified Authenticated AI-Assisted Literature Search

**Purpose**: Validate the completeness, clarity, consistency, and measurability of authentication, Row-Level Security (RLS), atomic daily quota, shared cache protection, and 3-tier AI failover requirements before `/speckit-tasks` and implementation.
**Created**: 2026-11-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | [plan.md](../plan.md) | [data-model.md](../data-model.md) | [contracts/ai-search-route-and-ui.md](../contracts/ai-search-route-and-ui.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Authentication & Access Boundary Requirements

- [ ] CHK001 Are the authentication boundaries explicitly separated between 100% public standard search (`/search`) and server-authenticated AI synthesis (`/api/ai-search`) without ambiguity? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the rejection order for unauthenticated callers on `/api/ai-search` specified so `401 Unauthorized` is mandated before cache lookups, quota checks, or AI generation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, Contract §3.2]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the OAuth sign-in prompt requirements for signed-out visitors on `/` and `/search` clear about preserving the user's intended query and relative return destination without open-redirect risk? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, Contract §1]
- [ ] CHK004 Are role-based access rules for standard `member` vs. `admin` accounts unambiguously defined across both quota status reads (`GET`) and synthesis mutations (`POST`)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, Data Model §2.1]

## Input Validation, Prompt-Injection & Egress Guardrails

- [ ] CHK005 Are query length bounds (`3`–`300` characters), whitespace trimming, and invalid filter rejection rules consistently specified across client forms and server Zod validation? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, Contract §2]
- [ ] CHK006 Does the spec define explicit refusal and grounding requirements when a user submits off-topic, medical-dosing, or prompt-injection text inside a valid-length query? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK007 Are column-projection restrictions (`AI_CITATION_STUDY_COLUMNS` excluding `abstract_text` and `embedding`) and the `<2,000`-token context ceiling quantified with deterministic trimming rules for oversized study fields? [Measurability, Spec §FR-009, Data Model §3]
- [ ] CHK008 Are requirements defined for how inline `[S1]`..`[S5]` citations are validated or constrained so ungrounded or fabricated study identifiers cannot be surfaced? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, Gap]

## Shared Cache Integrity & Atomic Daily Quota Requirements

- [ ] CHK009 Are deterministic query-normalization rules (casing, whitespace, trailing punctuation, and canonical filter serialization) specified with sufficient precision to guarantee identical cache keys across equivalent requests? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, Research §2]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the execution order between shared cache lookup and atomic daily quota deduction unambiguously defined so cache hits (`< 1s`) never decrement user quota? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK011 Are allowed values (`7` vs. `30` days), default retention (`7` days), and natural expiration behavior (no purge on daily study ingestion) consistently documented across spec, data model, and environment contracts? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, Spec §Assumptions, Contract §4]
- [ ] CHK012 Are PostgreSQL RLS policies and direct-table write revocations (`REVOKE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE`) specified for `public.ai_search_cache` and `public.user_ai_daily_quotas` to prevent client tampering or cache poisoning? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, Data Model §1.1, Data Model §1.2]
- [ ] CHK013 Are concurrency and race-condition requirements (parallel tabs, double-clicks, simultaneous identical queries) explicitly addressed via atomic single-statement quota reservation (`check_and_increment_ai_quota`)? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Data Model §2.2]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the UTC daily reset boundary and the quota-exceeded (`429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED`) user messaging—including continued access to standard search and already-cached AI answers—clearly specified? [Clarity, Spec §US3-3, Contract §3.2]

## Multi-Tier Failover & Non-Penalizing Recovery

- [ ] CHK015 Are the exact ordered inference tiers (`Groq` → `OpenRouter :free` → `Gemini Free Tier`) and environment-configurable model identifiers/timeouts consistently specified across spec, plan, and contracts? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, Contract §4]
- [ ] CHK016 Are the HTTP failure conditions that trigger automatic tier failover (`429`, `5xx`, missing tier key, connect/TTFB timeout, empty stream) exhaustively enumerated? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012, Research §5]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the pre-stream commit boundary (awaiting first valid content token before streaming to client) specified to prevent partial/corrupted output from leaking across tier retries? [Clarity, Research §5, Gap]
- [ ] CHK018 Are non-penalizing quota refund requirements (`refund_ai_quota`) and zero-caching rules explicitly defined for both `0`-study matches and total 3-tier failure (`503 ALL_TIERS_FAILED`)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011, Spec §FR-013, Contract §3.2]
- [ ] CHK019 Does the contract specify recovery and quota-refund behavior if an active SSE stream fails mid-generation after emitting the `meta` event? [Edge Case, Contract §3.2]

## Acceptance Criteria Measurability & Route Scope

- [ ] CHK020 Are all security, quota, context-budget, and failover success criteria (`SC-001`, `SC-003`, `SC-004`, `SC-005`) stated with objective, quantifiable pass/fail thresholds? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–SC-005]
- [ ] CHK021 Are route-scope constraints (strictly 8 user-facing page routes and 2 internal Route Handlers, with `/guidelines` never mutated) consistently enforced across spec, plan, and contracts? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014, Contract §1]
- [ ] CHK022 Are all external API key and free-tier configuration assumptions (`GROQ_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `AI_DAILY_QUOTA_LIMIT`, `AI_CACHE_TTL_DAYS`) documented with safe fallback defaults? [Dependencies & Assumptions, Spec §Assumptions, Contract §4]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
